subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm designing a futuristic armored truck module using a builder SDK, planning the chassis, wheel joints, turret with yaw/pitch, and decorative elements like neon glow and screens before writing the actual TypeScript code.

Working out dimensions and joint placement...

For the paint job, I'm planning a dark gunmetal countershade with panelled rivet texture from the clockwork kit, plus hazard stripes on the bumper and neon magenta/cyan glow rods. I'm also sketching out texture decals—unit numbers, warning triangles, a HUD screen, emblems—and listing the main components to build: chassis frame with axles and driveshaft, then the hull loft.

Now I'm mapping out the rest of the vehicle: an armored cab with raked windscreen and glowing visor strip, hinged doors, a sloped hood with vents and ERA bricks, a ram-wedge front bumper with spikes and winch, a rear turret with twin railgun barrels and sensor dome, side skirts with fender arches and mud flaps, and finally the wheel assemblies.

Writing wheel geometry...

Calculating wheel placement and width to keep them outside the hull, then sketching fender boxes and arched torus geometry above each wheel to form the wheel wells.

Now I'm shifting to the cab design, placing a cab-over box forward on the hull with a lower body section and an upper greenhouse-style frustum shape for the windshield area.

Still working out cab geometry...

Placing door hinge joints and panels on both sides, then shaping the hood with a tapered nose block extending the hull forward with a sloped front.

Front end gets a bumper with spikes and hazard paint, glowing headlight slits, a dark grille with rods, and a winch; rear gets an armored cargo module with a turret mount, thruster bells, and a red glowing tail light strip.

Still working through the turret geometry, I'm setting up the yaw and pitch joints, ring and drum base, cheek armor, twin forward-facing barrels with glow coils and muzzle brakes, checking clearance over the cab roof.

Now I'm placing the rest of the greebles: lightbar, dome sensor, whip antennas, dish, and missile pods on the cargo module's top sides angled forward-up, plus side skirt plates with bolts, fuel tanks between the first and second axles, and vertical exhaust stacks behind the cab.

I need to check the exhaust stacks don't collide with the module front, so I'm nudging them slightly outward and back. I'm also spacing out the three wheel axles along z with the front pair getting a steering joint, and planning decals for unit numbers, warnings, and branding on the module and doors.

For the HUD screen, since the cab rear is blocked by the module, I'll place it on the module's rear hatch with a glow effect instead, plus a smaller unit-number panel on the side planes using the appropriate orientation so the text reads correctly from outside. Now I'm defining the hull paint scheme with a countershaded base color.

Still writing paint logic...

I'm settling on about 5-6 textures (decal, warning, brand, HUD, plate) and planning a scattering of small greeble boxes on the module top for visual detail, keeping the part count around 14. Now I'm writing helper functions for creating boxes and cylinders with configurable dimensions, color, bone attachment, and rotation to speed up assembling the model.

Still writing helpers...

Refining wheel proportions...

I'm budgeting part counts per wheel assembly to stay under the total limit, then planning the arches, mudflaps, suspension components like axle rods, differential pumpkin, leaf springs and shocks, plus underglow neon strips along the hull and flanks.

For the hull shape itself, I'm defining loft stations along the body with varying width and height from front to rear, smoothing them with a catmull curve anchored to the chassis bone, and setting the wheel hub radius.

Now I'm checking wheel placement against the hull width to avoid overlap—adjusting the wheel x-offset to 1.28 so the tire (0.44 wide) clears the hull bottom, and planning wheel arches at the outer edge. Moving on to defining the cab extrusion outline.

Setting up the cab extrusion and door panel positions...

Adding a roof panel, a lightbar with glow lamps, a dome sensor, and antenna whips on top, plus deciding to give the windscreen glass a dark cyan tint with a glowing HUD strip rather than transparency, then starting on a hood block beneath the front windscreen.

Working out the hood slope, grille plate with glow bars, headlight slits, and front bumper placement...

Adding module details now: inset side panels, vents, neon edge strips, decal numbering, sensor cluster, and a rear hatch with HUD screen and warning markings, plus glowing red thruster bells lathed at the rear and a license plate.

Now I'm building the top turret assembly — yaw and pitch joints, a ring and drum, cheek armor boxes, a cradle housing, and barrels extending forward as the muzzle.

Placing missile pods on the roof with slight tilt, checking they clear the turret ring, and adding tube caps with spike noses on the front face, then positioning cylindrical fuel tanks along the sides.

Checking that the side fuel tanks sit in the gaps between the wheel axles without colliding with wheel edges front and rear, and adding retaining straps as torus shapes before sketching skirt plates further out than the wheels.

Scrapping that skirt idea, I'm placing side armor plates between the wheels on the hull flanks with bolt details and hazard-stripe corners, plus small mudflaps behind each wheel and torus-based wheel arches, then adding a couple of swept cable details from roof to turret using catmull-rom curves.

Now I'm positioning twin exhaust stacks near the cab rear with heat shields, working out their radius and offset so they clear the hull module, then adding a whip antenna and a dish mounted on a lathe-generated base aimed off-axis on the rear roof module, plus a camera-eye sensor ball up front.

I'm defining the color palette for tires, rims, steel trim, dark accents, and glow colors like cyan, magenta, amber, and red. I'm naming the six wheels by position, assigning hinge roles to doors and chassis joints, and double-checking the overall height and lowest point of the rig to confirm the proportions work.

Now I'm starting to write out the actual TypeScript module, setting up part placements for decals with bone positions, directions, and texture mapping, plus glow wrappers for lit elements and hazard-striped bumper boxes. I'm moving into writing texture definitions next.

Writing texture SVGs...

I'm thinking through greeble details using randomized box placement on module tops, and sketching out a hull loft call that generates the chassis body from station profiles with a solid hull color.

Stations need at/w/h fields, plus frame rails and crossmembers underneath. Now writing the final version, aiming for roughly 350 lines.
